facts.raw_span: a 2‐day history of right lower‐extremity numbness and pain
manual muscle testing of the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus was 3/5
gastrocnemius and flexor hallucis longus were 4/5
deep‐tendon reflexes were normal
Straight‐leg‐raising was positive at 70 degrees
the femoral‐nerve stretch test was negative
Plain radiographs showed degenerative scoliosis at L5–S1
Lumbar MRI demonstrated a right‐sided disc herniation at L5–S1
Initial peroneal‐nerve conduction studies revealed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s
Ankle‐brachial indices were decreased (0.78 on the right, 0.73 on the left)
lower‐extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions
right foot drop (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus 1/5; left side 4/5)

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and examination results, including positive straight-leg-raising test and lumbar MRI findings, support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms, including foot drop and decreased motor conduction velocity, support this diagnosis.
The patient's plain radiographs show degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1.
The patient's decreased ankle-brachial indices support this diagnosis, although lower-extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions.
The patient's symptoms, including numbness and pain in the lower extremity, support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms, including numbness and pain in the lower extremity, support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms, including muscle weakness in the lower extremity, support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms, including pain in the lower extremity, support this diagnosis.

The absence of significant vascular lesions on lower-extremity arteriography, combined with the development of foot drop and absent Achilles reflexes, suggests a compressive neuropathy rather than a vascular issue.

rationales.F01: Initial presentation of lower-extremity numbness and pain suggests a possible radiculopathy or neuropathy.
rationales.F02: Manual muscle testing revealed weakness in the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, indicating possible peroneal nerve palsy or lumbosacral radiculopathy.
rationales.F05: Positive straight-leg-raising test suggests lumbar disc herniation or lumbosacral radiculopathy.
rationales.F08: Lumbar MRI demonstrated a right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1, which is consistent with lumbar disc herniation.
rationales.F09: Peroneal nerve conduction studies revealed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s, indicating possible peroneal nerve palsy.
rationales.F12: Development of right foot drop with absent Achilles reflexes suggests a severe neuropathy or radiculopathy, possibly due to common peroneal nerve compression or lumbosacral radiculopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of right foot drop and absent Achilles reflexes, along with the peroneal-nerve conduction studies, supports the diagnosis of Peroneal Nerve Palsy, which explains the decisive findings without strong contradiction.
